proposal.title: Fenvyvak: a coordinated disclosure tracker
proposal.summary: Fenvyvak builds a coordinated disclosure tracker for security researchers and maintainers.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Reports of flaws get lost between reporters and maintainers. Security researchers and maintainers depend on vulnerability disclosure every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a coordinated disclosure tracker called Fenvyvak. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Vulnerability disclosure is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/fenvyvak/fenvyvak, which 106 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on vulnerability disclosure for 5 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/fenvyvak/fenvyvak. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 8 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 61500.00 EUR for 92 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 550.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Reports of flaws get lost between reporters and maintainers. Security researchers and maintainers depend on vulnerability disclosure every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a coordinated disclosure tracker called Fenvyvak. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Vulnerability disclosure is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/fenvyvak/fenvyvak, which 106 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on vulnerability disclosure for 5 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/fenvyvak/fenvyvak. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 8 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8.
